display.headline: How you come across before you say anything
display.body: Analytical, service-oriented and precision-focused. Systems, routines and quality standards matter deeply.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Ascendant computed in Virgo.

display.headline: What you are actually driving at
display.body: Core identity seeks variety, ideas and exchange.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Sun sign placement: Gemini (0.29 deg).

display.headline: How you settle yourself
display.body: Emotional rhythm is detached and objective, preferring conceptual distance.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Moon sign placement: Aquarius (19.97 deg).

display.headline: Your default way of deciding
display.body: 3 of your seven main planets sit in air signs, which is enough to set a house style. Under pressure, and with no time to think it through, you will think a decision through out loud, and change your mind when the argument changes. That is worth knowing mostly so you can tell when it is the right instinct and when it is just the loudest one.
display.tension: What you are drawn to does not match how you actually operate. Your momentum is air, but what attracts you runs fire, so the things you want and the way you go about getting them can quietly work against each other.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 25 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Dominant element: Air, carried by 3 of the seven classical planets.

display.headline: Where your chart is most crowded
display.body: More of your chart is stacked into one area of life than any other: home, roots and emotional foundations. Concentration like this tends to make a theme unavoidable rather than optional -- it is where the repeated events, the recurring lessons and the disproportionate share of your attention end up going.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: House 4 in Capricorn carries Saturn, Rahu.

display.headline: The engine your life actually runs on
display.body: The planet in charge of your whole chart is Mercury, and where it sits decides where your life keeps steering: shared resources and transformation. Of everything in a chart, this is the single clearest signal for what you will end up organising your years around, whether or not you chose it deliberately.
display.tension: This one grows through pressure rather than ease. Your main line of development runs through the harder rooms of the chart, so expect hidden effort, repeated restarts and a fair amount of work nobody sees before the outside picture matches the inside one.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 2 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Mercury rules Virgo and is placed in Taurus, house 8.

display.headline: Where you go looking for reassurance
display.body: Your attention keeps returning to creativity, romance and children whenever you need to feel steady. This is less about what you value in principle and more about where you instinctively go when something has knocked you off balance and you want the ground back under you.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Moon placed in Aquarius, house 5.

display.headline: What you are hungry for, and what you are done with
display.body: One end of this axis pulls you toward home, roots and emotional foundations with an appetite that rarely feels fully satisfied. The other asks you to loosen your grip on career, authority and public standing, which is usually the area you are already good at and can hide in. The pull and the release are the same mechanism.
display.tension: Both ends misbehave when they run unsupervised. Chasing too hard makes urgency outrun judgement; letting go too easily looks like maturity but is often just avoidance wearing better clothes.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Rahu in Capricorn, house 4; Ketu in Cancer, house 10.

display.headline: Your life happens out loud
display.body: 4 of your planets sit on the four corners of the chart -- the positions tied to self, home, partnership and public standing. Charts weighted this way tend to produce visible, eventful lives that respond quickly to decisive action, and respond just as quickly to indecision.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 19 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Planets in kendras: Venus, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu.

display.headline: People tend to meet you with goodwill
display.body: Jupiter -- the planet classically read as protection, good judgement and generosity -- falls directly on the part of your chart that describes you. In practice that tends to show up as people giving you the benefit of the doubt, second chances arriving when you need them, and a habit of looking for the meaning in a setback before looking for someone to blame. It is one of the quieter advantages a chart can carry.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 33 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Jupiter in house 9 (Gemini): in the lagna, or aspecting it by its 5th, 7th or 9th drishti.

display.headline: Saturn is on home ground
display.body: Saturn sits in a sign it governs, so your discipline, patience and relationship with limits behaves consistently rather than in bursts. This is not the most dramatic placement in a chart, but it is one of the most trustworthy: what it promises on a good day is roughly what it delivers on an average one.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 14 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Saturn placed in Capricorn, house 4.

display.headline: Saturn does its best work on the second pass
display.body: Saturn was moving backwards in the sky when you were born -- retrograde, in astrology's term. Classical texts treat a retrograde planet as strong but unconventional: your discipline, patience and relationship with limits tends to work inward first, revisiting and revising before it commits, and to find its own route rather than the expected one. What looks like hesitation from the outside is usually thoroughness.
display.tension: The trap is mistaking the review for the result. At some point the revision has to be finished and put in front of people, even if it could still be improved.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 36 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Saturn retrograde (vakri) in Capricorn, house 4.

display.headline: How your working life is built
display.body: Nurturing professions suit you best. Healthcare, hospitality, real estate, food industry, or counseling align with your protective nature.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: 10th house sign: Cancer. Lord Moon placed in house 5 in Aquarius.

claims.label: 10th lord placement
claims.detail: The 6th, 8th and 12th are the houses of effort, disruption and loss.

display.headline: Your work is where people find you
display.body: Ketu sit directly in the part of your chart that governs profession and public standing, which pushes their qualities straight into how you are seen at work. Careers with this signature tend to be less separable from identity than most -- what you do and who you are keep collapsing into the same answer.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 33 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Planets in 10th house (Cancer): Ketu.

display.headline: You do your best work against a deadline or a rival
display.body: One of the hard-edged planets sits in the part of your chart that governs competition, service and the daily grind -- one of the few places classical astrology actually wants them. Pressure there sharpens you rather than wearing you down: you tend to outlast competitors, take on the problems other people walk away from, and get better at difficult work every year you do it. Work built on competition, service, health, law or repair suits it well.
display.tension: The risk is needing an opponent to feel motivated. Without a rival or a crisis the same energy can turn inward as restlessness, or go looking for a fight that was never necessary.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 35 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: 6th house (Pisces) holds Mars: a natural malefic in a dusthana that is also an upachaya.

display.headline: What you are actually looking for in a partner
display.body: Romantic, empathic and spiritually connected in love. You seek a soulmate bond, creative expression, and emotional transcendence.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: 7th house sign: Pisces. Lord Jupiter in house 9 (Gemini).

display.headline: How you show affection, as opposed to how you feel it
display.body: Venus is the part of a chart that governs attraction and how care actually gets expressed. In Aries it runs through fire habits, which shapes what reads as love when you give it -- and, more usefully, explains why affection you offered sincerely has sometimes not landed as affection at all.
display.tension: How you express desire and what you want from commitment are made of different material -- fire against water. Left unexamined this shows up as choosing people you are drawn to over people you would actually be well matched with.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Venus at 24.91 deg in Aries, house 7.

display.headline: Romance and creativity run on the same circuit
display.body: Moon occupy the part of your chart that handles play, romance and creative output. These tend to move together for you: periods where you are making something are usually periods where you are more open to being pursued, and creative droughts and romantic ones often arrive in the same month.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 32 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: 5th house in Aquarius with Moon.

display.headline: Teachers and beliefs carry more weight for you than average
display.body: The part of your chart dealing with belief, higher learning and long-range good fortune is occupied rather than empty. Charts like this tend to have identifiable turning points attached to a particular teacher, a particular book, or a period abroad -- influence arriving from outside your existing world rather than from inside it.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 13 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: 9th house in Taurus with Sun, Jupiter.

display.headline: Saturn is one of the pillars of your chart
display.body: Saturn is both in one of its strongest signs and on one of the four corners of your chart, the combination classical astrology counts among its five great-person patterns. It makes your discipline, patience and relationship with limits a defining feature rather than one trait among many: people tend to know you for it, and the parts of life that run on it are where you are most likely to stand out.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Sasa yoga: Saturn own sign in Capricorn, house 4 (a kendra).
